prompt: After the user clears data, which confirmation string follows the Brave voice guidelines?
choices: "Brave cleared your browsing history."
"Your browsing history has been cleared by the system."
"Browsing history clearing has been completed successfully."
"Poof! Your history is gone for good!"
explain: Use active voice (say who did it), stay concise and simple, and be friendly but not jokey or whimsical.

prompt: Which warning text follows the Brave style guide?
choices: "You cannot undo this action."
"You can't undo this action."
"This action cannot be undone."
"This action is not able to be undone."
explain: Use contractions where possible; they're more conversational and save space in UI strings.

prompt: An ad-reporting dialog needs a label for a flagged ad. Which is best?
choices: "This ad looks creepy"
"This ad is basically sketchy"
"This ad looks suspicious"
"This ad seems fishy"
explain: Avoid colloquial language, idioms, slang, and filler words like "basically"; they can confuse, offend, or translate poorly.

prompt: A consent checkbox appears before account creation. Which label follows the perspective rules?
choices: "You've read the Brave terms of service"
"The user has read the Brave terms of service"
"We confirm you've read our terms of service"
"I've read the Brave terms of service"
explain: Address readers in second person (you, your), but use first person (I, me, my) when the user takes an action or gives consent.

prompt: A privacy notice explains what search data is accessible. Which phrasing does the style guide prefer?
choices: "Brave can only access the following search data…"
"We can only access the following search data…"
"Our team can only access the following search data…"
"The following search data can only be accessed…"
explain: For legal, security, or data privacy topics, say "Brave" or "the Brave team" instead of "we" to avoid implying staff can access user data.

prompt: You're writing a Shields-down confirmation dialog. Which version best follows the sentence-length guideline?
choices: "Are you sure you want to put Shields down for this page? Shields down may reduce your privacy."
Title: "Put Shields down?" Body: "Shields down may reduce your privacy on this site."
"Putting Shields down for this page, which you may want to do, may reduce your privacy and expose trackers."
Title: "Are you sure you want to put Shields down for this page right now?"
explain: Aim for 15 words or fewer per sentence. Break long sentences up (e.g. a short title plus body) and read them aloud to test.

prompt: Which help text uses the preferred tense?
choices: "Clicking 'Search default' will show a list of search options"
"Once you click 'Search default,' you'll see a list of search options"
"Click 'Search default' to see a list of search options"
"You are clicking 'Search default' to be seeing search options"
explain: Default to simple present tense. If a verb follows was/were, has/have, is/are, or be, or ends in -ing, it isn't simple tense.

prompt: Which sentence follows the style guide's language guidance?
choices: "Ask the account owner to approve his request."
"Ask the account owner to approve his or her request."
"Ask the chairman of the account to approve the request."
"Ask the account owner to approve the request."
explain: Rephrase to avoid gendered pronouns (defaulting to they/their if unavoidable) and avoid gender-latent words like "chairman" or "policeman."

prompt: Which desktop settings section heading is correctly cased?
choices: "Clear browsing data"
"Clear All Browsing Data"
"CLEAR BROWSING DATA"
"clear browsing data"
explain: Use sentence case for headlines, titles, and buttons; never ALL CAPS. Title case is only for branded product names (iOS is an exception, following Apple's rules).

prompt: Which marketing line follows the style guide?
choices: "Keep your friends, Brendan and Brian, safe with Brave"
"Keep your friends, Brendan, and Brian safe with Brave"
"Keep your friends, Brendan & Brian safe with Brave"
"Keep your friends; Brendan; and Brian, safe with Brave"
explain: Always use the Oxford (serial) comma before the last item in a list of 3 or more.

prompt: Which string follows Brave's punctuation rules?
choices: "Loading..." using three standard periods
"Loading!!" with doubled exclamation for emphasis
"Loading…" with the Unicode ellipsis character
"Loading . . ." with periods spaced per print style
explain: Use the Unicode ellipsis `…`, not three periods. Exclamation points are used sparingly, never more than one per view.

prompt: Which sentence uses hyphens and dashes correctly per the style guide?
choices: "Keep a browser that's up-to-date. Support is available Monday - Friday."
"Keep an up to date browser. Support is available Monday to-Friday."
"Keep an up-to-date browser — support is available Monday-Friday."
"Keep an up-to-date browser. Support is available Monday–Friday."
explain: Hyphenate multi-word adjectives before a noun ("up-to-date browser"), not after. Use an en dash for spans replacing "to," and em dashes have no surrounding spaces.

prompt: Which confirmation modal follows the UI copy guidelines?
choices: Title "Delete history?", a body stating the consequence, button [Delete history]
Title "Would you like to delete your history now?" with buttons [OK] and [Cancel]
Title "Delete history?" with button [YES, DELETE THE HISTORY]
Title "Please confirm", body "Are you sure you want to continue?", button [Continue]
explain: Confirmation modals: the title states the action as a question, the body states consequences, and the button repeats the action verb (≤3 words, sentence case, no articles).

prompt: A page failed to load. Which error message meets the guidelines?
choices: "Whoopsie! Something went wrong. We're on it, hang tight!"
"This page failed to load. Try reloading, or setting Shields down."
"Sorry, the server failed to fetch the page. Please try again later."
"Invalid response from server (error code 502). Reload to retry."
explain: Error messages must say what happened and offer a solution; never a dead end. Avoid exclamations, apologies, "please," blame, and jargon like server, fetch, or invalid.

prompt: Which email footer text follows the accessibility guidance?
choices: "To unsubscribe from these emails, click here." (with "here" as the link)
"Click the link below to unsubscribe from future emails."
"Want to stop getting these emails? Unsubscribe." (link on "Unsubscribe")
"Unsubscribe using the button to the right of this message."
explain: Never use "click here" as link text; describe what happens. Also avoid directional language like "to the right of" or "below."

prompt: Which UI string formats numbers and dates correctly?
choices: "Sync three devices by June 1st at 6:00 PM"
"Sync 3 devices by 6/1/21 at 6:00pm"
"Sync 3 devices by June 1st at 18:00"
"Sync 3 devices by June 1 at 6:00 pm"
explain: In UI, use digits for 0–9. Dates have no ordinals or numeric formats, and times are lowercase with a space: "6:00 pm."

prompt: Which storage and pricing string is formatted correctly?
choices: "Get 1 TB for HK$9.99, 50% off"
"Get 1TB for $9.99 HKD, 50 % off"
"Get one TB for HK$9.99, 50 percent off"
"Get 1 TB for 9.99 HK$, 50% off"
explain: Put a space between a number and its unit ("1 TB"), no space before % ("50%"), and use the currency symbol with the country outside the US ("HK$9.99").

prompt: Which sentence follows Brave's product naming conventions?
choices: "Download the Brave Browser and turn on shields."
"Download the Brave browser and turn on Shields."
"Download Brave and turn on shields."
"Be Brave: download the Brave Browser today and turn on Shields."
explain: "Brave browser" always has a lowercase "browser," and Shields is always capitalized, even in general usage. Never use "Brave" as an adjective.

prompt: Which settings toggle label follows the style guide's word choices?
choices: "Activate Brave Private Ads"
"Enable Brave Private Ads"
"Turn on Brave Private Ads"
"Turn on Brave ads"
explain: Say "turn on"/"turn off," not "enable"/"disable," and use the branded names "Brave Ads" or "Brave Private Ads."

prompt: Which Brave Rewards and Playlist copy uses the approved vocabulary?
choices: "Tip BAT to creators. Download videos to your playlist."
"Donate BAT to creators. Save videos to your playlist."
"Send BAT to creators. Watch saved videos in your playlist."
"Contribute BAT to creators. Add videos to your playlist."
explain: Use "contribute"/"support" for BAT (not donate, tip, give, pay, or send), "add" for Playlist (not download/save), and "view" instead of "watch."

prompt: Which privacy claim follows Brave's terminology rules?
choices: "Brave routes your request through a proxy, so the site can't see your IP address."
"Your browsing is 100% anonymous thanks to our anonymizing server network."
"Military-grade encryption keeps your browsing completely private from everyone."
"Brave's TOR windows make you totally secure and invisible to every site you visit."
explain: Privacy claims must say specifically what's protected and how. Never use superlatives like "100% anonymous" or "military-grade," prefer "proxy server" over "anonymizing server," and never write "TOR."

prompt: Which string is best for localization?
choices: "Be sure to clear this page's contents"
"Clear the content of this page"
An "Aa" icon with no text label
A button image with the text "Clear" baked into the PNG
explain: Write for translation: lead with the verb (not "Be sure to…"), avoid possessives, avoid letters in icons, label icons with text, and keep text out of images.

prompt: Which Rewards balance string follows the BAT guidelines?
choices: "80 BAT points"
"80.00 BAT (cryptocurrency)"
explain: Show BAT balances to three decimal places, never with a currency symbol. BAT is a "token" or "crypto asset," never a point, currency, or cryptocurrency.

prompt: Which onboarding sentence describes devices correctly on first reference?
choices: "Sync bookmarks between your PC and your mobile device."
"Sync bookmarks between your laptop computer and your smartphone."
"Sync bookmarks between your desktop and your device."
"Sync bookmarks between your computer and your phone or tablet."
explain: Use "phone or tablet" on first mobile reference (then "your device"), and "computer" for non-mobile machines; avoid laptop, PC, or desktop.

prompt: Which marketing line follows Brave's product messaging rules?
choices: "Brave Talk: free video calls for up to 4 people, with no time limit."
"Brave Talk: end-to-end encrypted video calls for everyone, totally free."
"Brave VPN: watch your favorite streaming sites from anywhere."
"The Brave browser blocks all ads and trackers, unlike Meta."
explain: Talk can claim free calls for up to 4 people with no time limit, but never "E2E"/"end-to-end." Don't pitch VPN for streaming, claim Brave blocks ALL ads/trackers, or call out companies like Meta.
